status_summary: The program has continued and is being put on a regulatory footing rather than repealed. A 2025 law (Public Law 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) expanded the program's orphan drug exclusion, which narrows its reach but leaves it in place. CMS issued final guidance for the third cycle on 2025-09-30 (published in the Federal Register on 2025-11-28) and on 2026-01-27 announced 15 selected drugs, the first cycle to include Part B drugs, plus one drug selected for renegotiation, with negotiated prices taking effect 2028-01-01; for the second cycle CMS reported agreement on all 15 drugs, with prices effective 2027-01-01. On 2026-06-16 CMS proposed to codify the program in regulation (new 42 CFR part 429; comments closed 2026-08-17 and CMS expects a final rule in fall 2026) and on 2026-07-20 issued draft guidance on putting 2028 prices into effect. Separately, CMS finalized the GLOBE model on 2026-10-02, a mandatory Part B rebate model benchmarked to international prices that takes effect 2026-11-30 and excludes drugs with a negotiated price. No repeal bill advancing was found in searches through 2026-10-15. CMS's third-cycle fact sheet schedules the negotiation period to end 2026-11-01, and Health Affairs counts four of the 15 selected drugs as primarily Part B.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed (GovInfo dates it 2025-07-04); its section 71203 expands and clarifies the orphan drug exclusion in the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program. CMS's final guidance of 2025-09-30 (next entry) addresses it.

CMS issues final guidance for the third cycle (initial price applicability year 2028) and first renegotiation, continuing the program; the guidance was published in the Federal Register on 2025-11-28 (90 FR 54692).

CMS announces the third cycle: 15 selected drugs, the first to include Part B drugs, plus one previously negotiated drug (Tradjenta) selected for renegotiation, with prices effective 2028-01-01. CMS also reports agreement with manufacturers on all 15 second-cycle drugs, with prices effective 2027-01-01 and estimated savings of about $8.5 billion (about 36 percent) had they applied in 2024.

CMS proposes (docket CMS-4215-P) to codify the program in 42 CFR part 429 and adjust Part D rules: selection of up to 20 drugs across Part B and Part D from initial price applicability year 2029, rules on the orphan drug exclusion, biosimilar delay requests, renegotiation and a temporary price floor for small biotech drugs. Comments closed 2026-08-17 (11,341 received); CMS expects a final rule in fall 2026.
CMS publishes draft guidance (91 FR 45278) on how manufacturers put negotiated prices into effect in 2028; comments were due 2026-09-18.

CMS publishes the final GLOBE model rule (91 FR 62936, effective 2026-11-30): a mandatory Part B drug rebate model benchmarked to international prices, running from 2027-04-01; it excludes drugs that have a negotiated maximum fair price in effect and is separate from the negotiation program.

title: Repeal the Medicare drug price negotiation program created by the Inflation Reduction Act
uncertainties: Federal Register documents were read through summarizing fetches (the proposed rule and GLOBE rule were read only through the first 100,000 characters). The first-cycle (2026 prices) results were not examined, and the third-cycle selection summary is slightly unclear on whether the 15 drugs split between Part B and Part D (the CMS release is described as including the first Part B drugs). The orphan drug exclusion change comes from CMS's description of Public Law 119-21 section 71203; the statute text was not read. Manufacturer litigation over earlier cycles was not checked. The Mandate also says to be prudent in implementing the law; this record treats the orphan drug expansion as consistent with that and the Part B expansion and codification as inconsistent, which makes 'diverged' (0) a judgment call on the repeal recommendation rather than on the whole passage. Search terms in the Federal Register API: 'Medicare Drug Price Negotiation' since 2025-01-20. Re-check on 2026-10-15: the CMS fact sheet (printed March 2026) gives 2025-09-30 as the issue date of the final third-cycle guidance, which the Federal Register published on 2025-11-28; the timeline uses the issue date. The fact sheet does not list the maximum fair prices. The split of selected drugs (four primarily Part B) comes from Health Affairs, a secondary source. A Federal Register search from 2026-09-15 found only the GLOBE final rule and a Part D pharmacy contracting RFI; two web searches found no repeal bill advancing in 2026 (results were 2024 items and commentary on pill-penalty fixes, not read). The 340B rebate pilot lead was not examined (context only).
